sec: Anion gap parameters and the corrected anion gap · p829

items.q: Match the anion gap derivation — 1) measured cation + unmeasured cation  2) mc − ma  3) Anion gap  4) Formula … A) = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation  B) = measured anion + unmeasured anion  C) = uc − ua  D) = Na⁺ − (HCO₃⁻ + Cl⁻)
items.exp: measured cation + unmeasured cation = measured anion + unmeasured anion; rearranged as mc − ma = ua − uc, so anion gap = uc − ua = Na⁺ − (HCO₃⁻ + Cl⁻). (Book p829)

items.q: The normal anion gap is given as:
A patient has an anion gap of 10 mEq/L and a serum albumin of 2.0 g/dL. Using the printed formula, what is the corrected anion gap?
items.exp: AGc = AG + 2.5 (4.5 − S.albumin) = 10 + 2.5 (4.5 − 2.0) = 10 + 6.25 = 16.25 mEq/L, unmasking a high anion gap. (Book p829)

items.q: Which measured cation is used in the printed anion gap formula?
items.exp: AG = Na⁺ − (HCO₃⁻ + Cl⁻) — potassium is not included in the printed formula. (Book p829)

items.q: ‘The corrected anion gap is used because albumin contributes to the measured/unmeasured charge balance.’
opts: True — the correction AG + 2.5 (4.5 − S.albumin) adjusts for the albumin level
False — the correction adjusts only for phosphate
False — the correction adjusts for serum potassium
True, but the correction is applied only when albumin exceeds 4.5 g/dL
items.exp: AGc = AG + 2.5 (4.5 − S.albumin); a low albumin lowers the measured gap, so the corrected value unmasks a high anion gap. (Book p829)

items.q: All but one of these statements about the anion gap are printed on p829. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Unmeasured anions raise the gap while unmeasured cations also raise it
mc − ma = ua − uc provides the derivation
The normal anion gap is 12 ± 2 mEq/L
items.exp: The gap is unmeasured anion minus unmeasured cation, so unmeasured *cations* lower it — they do not raise it. (Book p829)
